A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VAGUE and multimodal intention disambiguation. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable. The supplied v1 ends with references; v2 includes supplementary Sections A-H. Substantial dataset and protocol revisions limit direct score comparisons but do not prevent comparison of the work.

before.justification: Section 5 and Tables 1-2 report original multiple-choice and free-response evaluations of eight models, prompting ablations and a person-tag recognition experiment.

after.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original evaluations of ten models on VCR and Ego4D subsets, CoT experiments and a human comparison on 400 selected items.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction procedure changes substantially. V1 describes model selection of indirect candidates with BERT-rank verification; v2 uses human selection and rating thresholds for direct and indirect expressions. V2 also generates distinct linguistic styles jointly with superficial-understanding distractors and adds YOLOv11 person annotation for Ego4D (Section 4). These change construction steps, without introducing a trained reasoning model.

E1.justification: V1's MID evaluation uses VCR-derived scenes. V2 adds 533 Ego4D examples representing natural, first-person interactions and evaluates this domain separately from VCR. Multiple-choice and free-response tasks remain, and the three-image COCO person-tag check is retained in Appendix B.4.

E2.justification: The roster changes from eight to ten models, with a new human comparator. ShareGPT-4v variants, LLaVA 1.5 and NeXT-Mistral are removed; Phi3.5, Onevision, Qwen2.5-VL, Idefics2, Ovis2 and previously excluded GPT-4o are added. InternVL2 configurations are replaced by InternVL-2.5-MPO. NeXT-Vicuna 13B and Gemini 1.5 Pro remain. CoT comparisons now include only GPT-4o and Gemini.

E3.justification: Evaluation changes to 1,144 VCR and 533 Ego4D items, with a selected 400-item human comparison. V1's six prompting configurations become LM/SM/VLM evaluations plus proprietary-model CoT; few-shot ICL, manual-CoT examples and BLEU-2 evaluation disappear. Appendix G explicitly counts refusals as incorrect using total-item denominators, unlike the valid-response denominators evident in v1's tables.

E4.justification: V2 revises visual-cue and distractor-error analyses and replaces v1's ICL/manual-CoT ablations with targeted comparisons of CoT under caption and image inputs. It adds action/object diversity analysis and free-form diagnostic examples, including an antonymy test of BERT-F1. V1's BERT-rank prompt-selection check disappears. The existing OCR check is retained and documented for the revised model roster.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. V2's annotation ratings and human sample size describe curation and evaluation design, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V1's results, including Gemini's 0.71 caption-plus-ICL accuracy in Table 2, are replaced by results on the re-curated subsets. V2 adds the human comparison, reporting 94.0% versus 63.0% for the best model, and new CoT results such as Gemini VLM accuracy changing from 60.6% to 64.4% (Tables 2-3). These are new or replaced measurements, not same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: Both retain the same conditional-argmax task definition in Equation 1 and the relevance, solvability, consistency and ambiguity criteria. V2 clarifies the setting and expands examples, but introduces no substantively different mathematical definition, theorem, proof or derivation.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes the benchmark, scalable generation pipeline and eight-model prompting evaluation. V2 recasts the contributions around human-validated data spanning staged and natural scenes, explicit visual dependency, and a measured human-model gap. Its abstract and conclusion elevate the distinction between perceiving visual cues and using them to infer intent into a central finding.

C2.justification: V2 explains proprietary models' caption advantage through reduced visual hallucination and interprets CoT benefits as improved grounding, replacing v1's emphasis on response failures and generally ineffective CoT. It adds English-only, cultural and generation-model bias limitations and more specific criticism of free-response metrics. V1's GPT-4o exclusion, multimodal few-shot and computational-resource limitations are removed.

D1.justification: V2 supplies generation and evaluation prompt templates, human rating rubrics and interfaces, annotator/subset details, and a sample data schema. It explicitly documents model-generated SM captions and YOLOv11 annotation. The code/data link is retained. Conversely, v1's instruction to remove the shared response prefix before similarity scoring is no longer stated; an actual preprocessing change cannot be established.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially repositioned from visual grounding and intention disambiguation within/beyond text to multimodal Theory of Mind and implicature understanding. V2 introduces discussions of MMToM-QA, BOSS, MuMA-ToM, multimodal humor and memes, while removing much of the grounding and text-disambiguation discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Experiments are reorganized around visual cues, failure modes, human comparison and CoT. Definitions are condensed, while model descriptions, OCR testing and free-response discussion move into an extensive supplement. The title and author information also change.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the motivating illustration, removes v1's benchmark-difficulty diagram, redraws the construction pipeline and restructures results around domain and visual-input comparisons. It adds human/CoT tables, diversity diagrams, examples, annotation interfaces and prompt displays. V1's OCR Figure 8 is retained as Figure B2; the result and distribution graphics undergo substantial redesign.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens benchmark validation and reproducibility through human filtering, explicit rubrics, detailed prompts, a complementary natural-scene domain and a human reference experiment, addressing important weaknesses in v1. Qualifications remain: the human reference uses one evaluator on selected items; Table 2 reports 94.0% despite listing 374 correct out of 400; and Figure H7 presents an explicit request as an indirect example. These limit the strongest validity claims but do not outweigh the substantial methodological and documentation gains.
